task: 2017 US state-level energy indicator correlation/PCA assessment + 2x3 multi-source figure -> output.png

panels: row0col0 PCA scatter of 51 states (PC1 vs PC2, color=residential electricity price, RdYlBu_r, colorbar label 'Residential Electricity Price (cents/kWh)', 8 state annotations, zero reference lines, explained-variance note)
row0col1 global bubble (renewable share x vs CO2 per capita y, bubble=population, n=172 countries 2019, xlim[0,100], ylim[0,30], 5 country labels, Qatar clipped note)
row0col2 pie of steel Load_Type distribution (Light 18072 / Medium 9696 / Maximum 7272, autopct)
row1col0 bar of Sunroof kW totals by granularity (State/County/City/Postal Code) with M labels
row1col1 horizontal bar of top-10 2017 fossil generation states (TX 341.8M MWh ... NC 73.3M)
row1col2 steel energy-usage time series, first 672 intervals (7 days at 15-min), weekend shaded

method.state_table: derived/state_2017_features.csv, 51 rows (50 states + DC), zero nulls in the 5 model columns
method.correlation: Pearson r (plus Spearman as rank-robustness check) over log_kw_total, yearly_sunlight_kwh_median, renew_share, res_price, fossil_share, deploy_per_1k, percent_qualified
method.pca: z-score (ddof=0) of [log_kw_total, yearly_sunlight_kwh_median, renew_share, res_price, fossil_share] -> SVD; signs fixed so PC1.renew_share>0 and PC2.res_price<0
method.global_panel: global-data-on-sustainable-energy.csv (2019) INNER JOIN owid-co2-data.csv (2019) on country, iso_code notna -> 172 countries
method.steel_panel: Steel_industry_data.csv, date parsed day-first (%d/%m/%Y %H:%M), sorted; pie over all 35040 intervals, line chart over first 672 points
method.granularity_panel: sum(kw_total) per Project Sunroof file after dropna(subset=['region_name'])
method.fossil_panel: US_Energy_Generation_2001-2022.csv: YEAR==2017, TYPE OF PRODUCER=='Total Electric Power Industry', ENERGY SOURCE in [Coal, Petroleum, Natural Gas, Other Gases], monthly sum, US-TOTAL dropped
method.priority_scoring: score_B = z(sunlight)+z(fossil_share)-z(deploy_per_1k)-z(renew_share); score_A = score_B + z(res_price); z with ddof=0 over 51 rows
method.rendering: matplotlib Agg, figsize (20,11), dpi 150, suptitle y=0.995, tight_layout(rect=[0,0,1,0.955], h_pad=4.5, w_pad=2.5), savefig bbox_inches='tight'

key_intermediate_results.pca_axis_reading: PC1(+) = renewable-heavy / fossil-light (VT 4.62 highest; DC, ME, SD); PC1(-) = fossil-heavy + large installed capacity (FL -2.58; LA, TX, AZ, NM). PC2 dominated by cheap electricity (res_price loading -0.69) and installed capacity (+0.46); WA/ID top PC2, HI/AK/RI bottom.
critical_findings: sunlight ~ res_price: r=-0.09 (Spearman -0.50) -> solar resource and electricity price are effectively decoupled; a price-only federal signal misses the sunniest states
fossil_share ~ sunlight: r=+0.30 -> the sunniest states are also the most fossil-heavy => highest abatement leverage
res_price ~ deploy_per_1k: r=+0.63 (Spearman 0.35) -> adoption follows high prices in level terms but rank-order is weaker (Hawaii-like outliers)
renew_share ~ fossil_share: r=-0.75 is largely mechanical (common Total-generation denominator) -> read as a single clean-vs-fossil axis
log_kw_total ~ renew_share: r=-0.36 -> absolute installable capacity concentrated in large fossil-heavy states

policy_conclusion.priority_tier_1: New Mexico, Mississippi, Florida, Louisiana, Delaware, Wyoming, Arizona, Missouri, Arkansas, Indiana (robust across both scoring variants): high irradiance + fossil-dominated mix + low current solar penetration -> 2017 federal incentive priority
policy_conclusion.priority_tier_2: Rhode Island and Hawaii enter only via the price term while irradiance is low -> target efficiency/equity programs rather than utility-scale solar
policy_conclusion.lowest_priority: Vermont, District of Columbia, Washington, Maine, Oregon (already clean or low irradiance)
policy_conclusion.caveat: carbon intensity is proxied by fossil generation share (no state emissions variable in the provided data); the ranking is weight-sensitive and is reported together with its four raw indicators

validation.text_overlap_check: automated pairwise text-bbox check -> 0 overlapping pairs

notes: matplotlib 3.11 / numpy 2.5 / pandas 3.1 used with sys.path.append to user site-packages under python3 -I
no seaborn used; all panels drawn with plain matplotlib
Qatar (36.3 t CO2/capita) falls outside the mandated ylim [0,30] and is annotated instead of rescaling
steel panel is single-plant 2018 data used as multi-dimensional context only; it does not enter the state priority score
